gen-gf-warnes-gf-major-mono-display: Major Mono Display glows like neon tubing, monospace and precise. Warnes sits above it with tapered ink strokes and stretched spacing, so the page swings between hand-inked boldness and glassy, technical order.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-matemasie: Warnes stretches its tapered, uniform strokes wide and open, while Matemasie's sans letters sit closed and tight with small entry points. A slightly larger heading would let that openness show.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-menbere: Flat, fineliner-like lines with tapered ends define Warnes. Menbere's sans lowercase stacks tall like rolled cord underneath, and that stark difference in texture is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-mitr: Mitr is a plain sans with almost no gap between x-height and cap height. Mitr stays compact and sturdy under Warnes, whose pipe-cleaner letterforms stretch out wide and loose above it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-momo-trust-display: Warnes draws its curves with no pinching, stretched wide and bold, over Momo Trust Display's drifting sans-serif letters. Text in that body would feel spacious and unhurried.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-mukta: Mukta is a sans with tall-bodied small letters, quietly upright. Mukta reads smoothly over a long passage, while Warnes above it keeps tracing its single thick thread.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-mukta-mahee: Joins that never thin out where strokes meet give Warnes a bold, rope-like look. Mukta Mahee follows with chunky, tall lowercase in a sans that matches that sturdiness without copying it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-mukta-malar: Mukta Malar tucks its ascenders short, a sans-serif that stays approachable under the rope-bodied curves of Warnes. The strongest quality is how sturdy it feels.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-mukta-vaani: Strokes as plain as stitched thread outline give Warnes its look. Mukta Vaani, a high-waisted sans, would crowd that heading if the heading shrank too small.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-narnoor: Blueprint-lettering boldness, drawn in constant line by Warnes, sits over Narnoor's short ascenders and big bowls. Narnoor keeps the sans-serif text grounded while the heading stretches out.
